```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r attach}
library(priogridR)
```

All conversion functions use a `priogrid::pg_config()` object as the source of
truth for spatial and temporal resolution.

```{r config}
config <- priogrid::pg_config(
  nrow = 18,
  ncol = 36,
  temporal_resolution = "1 year",
  start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
  end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

## Point-event data

For data frames, specify the coordinate columns. Observation dates are mapped
to the intervals defined by `config`.

```{r points}
events <- data.frame(
  longitude = c(10, 10.1, 20),
  latitude = c(50, 50.1, 60),
  event_date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-03-01", "2021-06-01")),
  fatalities = c(2, 3, 1)
)

event_counts <- pg_from_points(
  x = events,
  variable = "event_count",
  longitude = "longitude",
  latitude = "latitude",
  aggregation = "count",
  time_column = "event_date",
  config = config
)

event_counts
```

To aggregate a value column, provide `value` and an appropriate rule:

```{r point-values}
fatalities <- pg_from_points(
  x = events,
  variable = "fatalities",
  longitude = "longitude",
  latitude = "latitude",
  value = "fatalities",
  aggregation = "sum",
  time_column = "event_date",
  config = config
)
```

## Raster data

`pg_from_raster()` accepts a `terra::SpatRaster` or raster-file paths. Use
`aggregation` to describe how finer cells should be combined and
`disagg_method` when the source is coarser than the target grid.

```{r raster, eval=FALSE}
elevation <- pg_from_raster(
  x = "data/raw/elevation.tif",
  variable = "elevation",
  aggregation = "mean",
  return = "result",
  config = config
)
```

## General vector data

`pg_from_vector()` detects point, line, and polygon geometry automatically.
Available aggregation rules depend on the geometry type. Examples include
point counts, line length, polygon coverage, area-weighted means, and
area-weighted allocation of totals.

```{r vectors, eval=FALSE}
road_length <- pg_from_vector(
  x = "data/raw/roads.gpkg",
  variable = "road_length_m",
  aggregation = "length",
  geometry = "line",
  config = config
)

forest_share <- pg_from_vector(
  x = "data/raw/forest.gpkg",
  variable = "forest_share",
  aggregation = "area_share",
  geometry = "polygon",
  config = config
)
```

## NetCDF data

`pg_from_netcdf()` reads a NetCDF file or accepts an already-opened
`SpatRaster`. Layer time is taken from the raster when available or supplied
explicitly through `time`.

```{r netcdf, eval=FALSE}
precipitation <- pg_from_netcdf(
  x = "data/raw/precipitation.nc",
  source_variable = "precip",
  variable = "precipitation",
  aggregation = "mean",
  config = config
)
```

## Geographically indexed tables

`pg_from_table()` joins a table to polygon geography before transferring the
values. Use `area_weighted_sum` to allocate a source-region total among cells;
use `constant` when every intersecting cell should inherit the same value.

```{r tables, eval=FALSE}
population <- pg_from_table(
  x = population_table,
  variable = "population",
  value = "population_total",
  geography = districts,
  source_id = "district_id",
  geography_id = "district_id",
  aggregation = "area_weighted_sum",
  config = config
)
```

## Missing values and structural zeros

For point data, `keep_empty = TRUE` completes unobserved cells only for
aggregations with an interpretable zero: `count`, `presence`, and `sum`. It
does not replace missing means, minima, or maxima with zero.

## Writing results

```{r writing, eval=FALSE}
pg_write_result(event_counts, "data/processed/event_counts.csv")
pg_write_result(elevation, "data/processed/elevation.tif")
```
